Refuse short comment openers in the disclosure D-4 reader (#283)

TODO 255 records that the disclosure case with '<!-->' in
tools/test-build-site.py pins Python 3.14.4's HTMLParser reading of
that opener and fails under Python 3.14.7 in a side-by-side test.

Add SHORT_COMMENT, re.compile(r"<!---?>"), the same pattern as check 9
of tools/check-inline-code.py, and the exception ShortCommentRefused.
disclosure_d4_section() raises it, before it parses, on any text that
SHORT_COMMENT matches, so its result on these openers does not come
from the interpreter's HTMLParser; it still reads all other markup
with that parser. The refusal names the text found, '<!-->' or
'<!--->', without calling it a comment; SHORT_COMMENT matches that
text inside an attribute value too. check_disclosure_states() catches
only ShortCommentRefused and reports it as a failure line, so any
other exception from the reader passes out instead of becoming a case
result. A new case checks that catch for 2 exception classes only: it
passes d4_failures() a stand-in reader that raises, whose
ShortCommentRefused must become the failure line and whose ValueError
must pass out unchanged. So the case fails when the catch is widened
to take in ValueError, such as to except Exception, and passes when it
is widened only by classes that leave ValueError out, such as
AssertionError. The '<!-->' case now expects the refusal, and a new
'<!--->' case expects it too. A new '<!---->' case puts an Entry 5
label after the empty comment and the note after the label, and
expects the lacks-note failure, which it gives only if the reader does
not refuse the empty comment and reads the label as a tag that ends
D-4. The case does not show that the reader parses '<!---->' as a
comment: a reading of it as text gives the same result. The '<!-->'
case is a fixture brought up to date with a deliberate contract
change: the test's reader now refuses that opener.

The comment on SHORT_COMMENT and the docstring of
disclosure_d4_section() name the text '<!-->' or '<!--->' wherever it
stands. The comment says that Python 3.14.4's HTMLParser reads either
one in text as the start of a comment up to the next '-->' or '--!>',
when one follows, and inside an attribute value as part of the value,
and that TODO 255 does not record how Python 3.14.7 reads '<!--->'.
Check 9 of tools/check-inline-code.py, which searches a page's whole
text with the same pattern, now names the text found in its message,
as "the text '<!-->' in an HTML page", in place of "a comment that
opens as '<!-->'". Its docstring entry says that it refuses that text
wherever it stands, such as inside an attribute value; what check 9
refuses is unchanged. A new case in tools/test-inline-code.py puts
'<!-->' in an attribute value and requires that message.

Add .github/squash/283.txt, which holds this message byte for byte.
.python-version is unchanged.

Checks, from the repository root, with the outputs of Python 3.14.4:

- python3 -I tools/test-build-site.py prints
  "test-build-site: all 1125 cases passed." and exits 0.
- python3 -I tools/test-inline-code.py prints
  "test-inline-code: all 154 cases passed." and exits 0.
